answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed when its actions violate a shared rule, such as double-claiming the same task. A reputation graph can then weight votes by bonded stake and by links to identities with a clean history, rather than counting accounts equally. A quill may record each claim, while a pulse of periodic checks lets honest agents recover bonds. A vertex in the graph earns influence only through costly, sustained participation, so an attacker must lock up capital in every sybil and risks losing it.
